MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 17, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on June 17, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 12, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk/Director of Community Relations

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are
  the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiators are Dennis
  Wilberg and Keith Rattay.

City Council Minutes  1  June 17, 2013
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council gave direction to staff but no
reportable actions occurred in Closed Session.

Mr. Curley and Mayor Reardon notified the audience that item 23 (Social Host Ordinance) will
be moved forward on the agenda to be addressed after public comments.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Swim & Dive Team as
  2013 CIF Southern Section Division I Champions

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to Coach Yancey and the team
  members.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Pamela St. Pierre, M.V.: expressed concern that a Mission Viejo jewelry business owner is
operating illegally and unethically. She asked when the citizens will be able to rely on City
officials to stop the unlawful activity.

City Attorney Curley announced that the City does not license or exercise any regulations over
local businesses so the City has no jurisdiction to bring an enforcement action. He noted that the
agencies with jurisdiction are the Orange County Sheriff's Department and the District Attorney
or Ms. St. Pierre can take civil action.

Mark Moore, Nadadores Masters Director and Coach, San Juan Capistrano: announced that the
Nadadores are hosting the U.S. Masters Summer Nationals at the Marguerite Aquatics
Center. They are expecting over 1,200 swimmers, including Olympians, for the 5-day event
from August 7 to 11, 2013. Mr. Moore stated that the Nadadores are excited about this showcase
event and to working with the City in a joint effort.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that the Relay for Life was a very special event and Mission
Viejo is only $840 away from being number one in donations. She encouraged residents to visit
the Relay for Life website and donate to whichever team they'd like. She also discussed the
recent Fran Crippen Swim Meet of Champions and she invited the City Council Members to
attend the upcoming Masters Summer Nationals at the aquatics center.

City Council Minutes  2  June 17, 2013
 Carrie Payne, M.V.: expressed support for the City's crossing guards and she asked the Council
to consider what an important service they provide when addressing the subject of reducing the
crossing guard's hours.

Wil Garcia, M.V.: thanked the City Council for renovating the Tennis Center and Musco Electric
for upgrading the tennis court lighting on their own dime. He announced that the International
Wheelchair Doubles Masters will be held at the facility in November and he asked the Council to
consider adding money to the budget for shade covers at the tennis courts.

Anna T. Boyce, Dan Moncino and Margot Ferron, M.V.: stated that the Community Center
parking lot is extremely dark from dusk to dawn and they asked that money for additional
lighting be included in the budget.

Farid Saatchi, M.V.: stated that the City of Mission Viejo has denied his request for a second
hand dealer's license and he noted that it is difficult for him to keep up his business without that
license.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

23. Social Host Ordinance

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley provided the Council with an update on the City's Social Host
  Ordinance.

  Sgt. Eric Hendry: outlined a potential ordinance that will allow the City to provide penalties
  when deputies have to make multiple trips to a party house. Sergeant Hendry answered
  questions of the City Council regarding calls to loud or out of control parties and he stated
  that the Social Host Ordinance is a very effective tool for the Sheriff's Department.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she will bring the proposed penalties ordinance
  back to the City Council for consideration at the next meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 10 and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  June 17, 2013
  1. Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated May 24, 2013 in the Amount of $547,456.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated May 31, 2013 in the Amount of $2,125,281.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2013

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2013

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April
  2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for April 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2013-14

  Adopted Resolution 13-32 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2013-14 for
  Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center.)

12. Recognition and Appropriation of Property Tax Administration Fee Reimbursement

  Adopted Resolution No. 13-33 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget to Recognize
  Property Tax Administration Fee Reimbursement Revenue and Appropriate These
  Resources for Specific Needs.

City Council Minutes  4  June 17, 2013
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

13. Review of 2013-15 Proposed Budget

  City Manager Wilberg noted that the budget maintains all core services and programs at
  current levels. In addition, there is $1.2 million available to add to discretionary reserves or
  to allocate to additional programs in the City.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented an overview of the proposed
  budget.

  Staff members answered questions of the City Council.

  Mark Jones, President of the Nadadores Board of Directors, M.V.: stated that funding is
  critical to the current and future success of the Nadadores and noted that he is interested in
  expenditure of the park development funds for repairs at the Marguerite pool complex.

  James Montrella, M.V.: announced that four 90 year-olds are going to attempt to break the
  swimming world record at the upcoming Masters World Championships in August and he
  outlined the many programs that are offered at the Marguerite swim complex.

  Mary Lee Robinson, Vice President of the Oso Valley Greenbelt Association, M.V.: stated
  that the Oso Valley Greenbelt Homeowners Association requests that the City Council
  place money in next year's budget for extension of the median islands on La Paz from
  Marguerite to Olympiad.

  Chuck Robinson, M.V.: thanked the Council Members and staff for the time and effort that
  they put forth for the community. He echoed support for the Oso Valley Greenbelt
  Association's request for extension of the median islands up La Paz Road to Olympiad.

  Keith Ruhland, M.V.: stated that he thoroughly enjoys living in Mission Viejo and driving
  around the City is a visual delight. He echoed Mr. and Mrs. Robinsons' comments on the
  extension of median islands on La Paz Road.

  David Allen, M.V.: requested continued support and funding for the Mission Viejo
  Activities Committee to promote community events such as the Fourth of July Street Faire.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: recommended that the City Council look at cost-saving ideas
  for police services and requested that staff contact various Orange County agencies to
  obtain copies of their cost-saving measures.

  Robert David Breton, M.V.: proposed that the City develop a new overlook park on a hill
  where La Paz Road ends at Olympiad Parkway with dedicated park development funds, not
  with general funds. He further stated that higher-priority projects should be done first and

City Council Minutes  5  June 17, 2013
   the Community Services Commission can provide recommendations if the Council so
  desires.

  Helen Workun, M.V.: stated that she enjoys the KSBR Breakfast with Gary and Kelly TV
  and radio show which brings people and artists from outside of the community to enjoy our
  City. Ms. Workun asked the City Council to please consider continued funding of the
  program.

  Anna T. Boyce, Dan Moncino, and Margot Ferron, M.V.: asked the City Council to provide
  funding for 4 bocce ball courts at the Murray Community and Senior Center.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: requested funding for the Nadadores swim complex and dive
  towers and that priority be given to the facility. She expressed her support for the City's
  crossing guards and, adding comments as a Community Services Commissioner, she noted
  that the Commission supports the extension of the Oso Creek Trail from Jeronimo up to
  Casta del Sol Drive.

  Carrie Payne, M.V.: reiterated her prior comments and asked the Council to revisit the
  budget for the crossing guard contract and maintain the current hours.

  A written comment was submitted by James Farber, M.V., expressing support for budget
  consideration of a landscaped median on La Paz Road for reasons of beautification of the
  street and for better traffic control.

  A written comment was submitted by Mary Lou Moncino, M.V., expressing support for
  upgraded lighting at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, as well as
  bocce ball courts.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  approve the proposed budget and direct staff to place the 2013-2015 budget on the July 1,
  2013, City Council agenda for adoption.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council directed that the following additional items be included in
  the 2013-15 Budget:

  1. Funding for the Wounded Warriors event in the amount of $6,000 in each fiscal year.

  2. Funding for the Community Campout in the amount of $4,500 in each fiscal year.

City Council Minutes  6  June 17, 2013
   3. Increased funding for the KSBR radio/television programs in the amount of $10,000 in
  FY 2013-14 only. The Council asked KSBR to seek sponsorship funding for future
  programs beyond FY 13-14.

  4. Funding for a Crown Valley Parkway public art project in the amount of $27,200 in FY
  2013-14.

  5. Increased educational reimbursements in the amount of $8,000 in each fiscal year.

  6. Increased professional development funding in the amount of $10,000 in each fiscal
  year.

  7. Funding for Middle School programs at the Potocki Center in the amount of $35,000 in
  each fiscal year.

  The City Council directed the Community Services Commission to evaluate a SVUSD
  Middle School Fitness Program and to conduct a pilot program.

  By consensus, the Council deferred any vote on projects that can be funded with park
  development fees until the Community Services Commission can review and recommend a
  prioritized list of projects.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas discussed the City's unfunded pension
  liability issue and the retiree health insurance program and answered the City Council
  Member's questions.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:53 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:05
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

14. Review of Council Policy 0300-8 Management and Budget Policies

  By consensus, the City Council deferred this item to the next meeting.

15. Annual Routine Street Sweeping Service

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the Council directed staff to amend paragraph 1 of the contract to make it
  clear that a contract extension is unilateral at the City's option, rather than mutual.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  award a contract for the subject services to Sunset Property Services for the period of July
  1, 2013, through June 30, 2015, in the amount of $671,168.00, as amended; (2) authorize
  staff to issue a purchase order to Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1, 2013,

City Council Minutes  7  June 17, 2013
   through June 30, 2014, in an amount not to exceed $335,584.00 pending adoption of the
  Fiscal Year 2013-2015 budget by the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the comments attributed to her on page 9, item 17, are
  the direct opposite of what she said. She noted that she did not suggest reducing the number
  of officers but that and there are other opportunities in the contract to reduce costs.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  Minutes for regular City Council Meeting of June 3, 2013, as presented, pending the City
  Clerk's review of Council Member Schlicht's comments on item 17 (page 9.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

10. Request by the Friends of the Mission Viejo Dog Park for a One-Time Exemption to
  the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City Facilities

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she does not support this exemption because
  alcohol should not be the center of our entertainment.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  request by the Friends of the Mission Viejo Dog Park for a onetime Exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation for a fundraising event held in the Kershaw
  Garden at the Mission Viejo Civic Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  June 17, 2013
 11. Claim Against the City - Baker & Unnamed Minor vs. City of Mission Viejo

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that Animal Services did not impound a
  vicious dog right away and that there might be overreaction from a prior case. She stated
  that the Council needs to take a look at the Animal Services policies.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  reject claim(s).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

17. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

18. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

19. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented a brief report and stated that he will give more detail at the
  next meeting.

20. SCAG Transportation and Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

Orange County Vector Control Agency Report

Council Member Leckness presented the report.

City Council Minutes  9  June 17, 2013
 21. Economic Development Committee Update

  Council Members Leckness announced that he and Council Member Schlicht will defer the
  report to the next City Council Meeting in the interest of time.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht invited residents to the Saddleback Republican Assembly meeting on
Thursday, June 20 at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. Guest speakers will be City of
San Juan Capistrano Council Member Derek Reeve and Capistrano Common Sense editor Kim
McCarthy who will present a program on how they are informing their voters. Council Member
Schlicht read a quote from Lyn Nofziger: "As I watch government at all levels daily eat away at
our freedom, I keep thinking how prosperity and government largesse have combined to make
most of us fat and lazy and indifferent to, or actually in favor of, the limits being placed on that
freedom." Council Member Schlicht stated that she can't believe the budget was passed without
much discussion.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he did not have any comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked all those who came out to donate at the recent blood drive. She
noted that there were 44 pints of blood collected, which could potentially help or save 132
lives. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed her attendance at the Community of Character Youth
Committee gala and she commended the young people who did such a fantastic job in planning
the event.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon outlined her attendance at the Capistrano Valley High School graduation and she
noted that the Scholar of Scholars is one of our Community of Character members, Zachary
Yee. She also announced that the Mission Viejo High School football team is seeking veterans
and active duty men and women from all service branches to be honored at a football game on

City Council Minutes  10  June 17, 2013
 October 25, 2013. Mayor Reardon announced that there will be a Dog Park fundraiser on July
13 in the Kershaw Garden at the Civic Center beginning at 6:00 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person
and are available online or by calling (949) 470-3014. Lastly, Mayor Reardon commended the
dog park supporters for their efforts to raise money for the new park.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 12:03 a.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, July 1, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 1, 2013

City Council Minutes  11  June 17, 2013
